newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Air NZ to buy half of Ansett for total A$475 mln.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ to buy half of Ansett for total A$475 mln.

text.p: Air New Zealand Ltd said on Monday it had agreed to buy 50 percent of Australia's Ansett Holdings from TNT Ltd for a total of A$475 million or about NZ$540 million.
Air NZ said it would fund the purchase with about NZ$350 million of its existing cash reserves and NZ$190 million of new borrowings.

It expects to raise about $240 million through a three-for-eleven rights issue at NZ$2.00/share. The new shares (about 121 million in total) will not qualify for the final 1996 dividend but will rank fully with existing shares for future dividends.
The company expects to maintain annual dividends of 20 NZ cents/share on the expanded capital base.
After the equity raising, the company's equity ratio will be about 47 percent and net debt to net debt plus equity will be around 28 percent.
The proportion of "B" shares in Air NZ -- those buyable by foreigners -- will increase to 49 percent from 35 percent in line with Australian ownership policy.
The rights issue will involve a pro rata issue of "A" shares (buyable only by New Zealanders) to A shareholders and B shares to B shareholders at the same price. The issue will not be underwritten.
Air NZ reiterated it expects the earnings impact of the Ansett investment to be relatively neutral in the short term.

"The strategic move to full involvement in an Australasian regional aviation market rather than a solely New Zealand-based market is critical to the future development of Air New Zealand," Chairman Bob Matthew said.

The deal also involves the sale of Ansett New Zealand to News Ltd and 51 percent of Ansett International Ltd to a consortium of Austrlian institutional investors, to ensure the overall transaction complies with regulatory requirements in both New Zealand and Australia.
